<|det|>title [105, 321, 250, 352]<|/det|>Severity
<|det|>text [136, 365, 285, 386]<|/det|>Impact: High
<|det|>text [136, 404, 320, 424]<|/det|>Likelihood: Low
<|det|>title [105, 445, 307, 475]<|/det|>Description
<|det|>text [135, 488, 755, 509]<|/det|>To calculate token00verToken1 for tokens that accrue value,
<|det|>text [135, 512, 905, 575]<|/det|>swapStorage.perSecondInterestRate is used to adjust the base price of the asset. Depending on the order of the tokens, this value can be positive or negative.
<|det|>text [135, 594, 929, 636]<|/det|>However, this approach is flawed, as applying a negative interest rate over the inverse price does not yield the correct result.
<|det|>text [136, 655, 473, 675]<|/det|>Consider the following example:
<|det|>list [129, 696, 922, 907]<|/det|>
<|det|>text [130, 696, 451, 716]<|/det|>○ XYZ is token0 (6 decimals).
<|det|>text [130, 720, 468, 740]<|/det|>○ AUSD is token1 (6 decimals).
<|det|>text [130, 745, 679, 763]<|/det|>○ XYZ price is $2 and its annual interest rate is 50%.
<|det|>text [130, 768, 922, 812]<|/det|>- token00VerToken1 is set to 0.5e18 (1/2 * 1e18) and annualizedInterestRate is set to -0.5e18 (negative 50% interest rate).
<|det|>text [130, 816, 898, 860]<|/det|>○ After 1 year, XYZ price is $3, so token00OverToken1 should be ~0.33e18 (1/3 * 1e18).
<|det|>text [130, 865, 901, 907]<|/det|>- token00OverToken1 is calculated as 0.5e18 * (1 - 0.5) = 0.25e18, which is incorrect.
